name: Parrot
para: Parrots are vibrant, intelligent birds known for their ability to mimic sounds and their complex social behaviors, with around 389 species found primarily in tropical and subtropical regions.

name: Owl
para: Owls are birds from the order Strigiformes[1] (/ˈstrɪdʒəfɔːrmiːz/), which includes over 200 species of mostly solitary and nocturnal birds of prey typified by an upright stance, a large, broad head, binocular vision, binaural hearing, sharp talons, and feathers adapted for silent flight.

name: Crow
para: Crows are intelligent birds belonging to the genus Corvus, which includes species like the American crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) and the carrion crow (Corvus corone)

name: Woodpecker
para: Woodpeckers are part of the bird family Picidae, which also includes the piculets, wrynecks and sapsuckers

name: Peacock
para: Peacock is a common name for two bird species of the genus Pavo and one species of the closely related genus Afropavo within the tribe Pavonini of the family Phasianidae (the pheasants and their allies)

name: Vulture
para: A vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion. There are 23 extant species of vulture (including condors).

name: Penguin
para: Penguins are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Kingfisher
para: Kingfishers are a family, the Alcedinidae, of small to medium-sized, brightly coloured birds in the order Coraciiformes.

name: Swan
para: Swans are birds of the genus Cygnus within the family Anatidae. The swans' closest relatives include geese and ducks.

name: Hen
para: The hen (Gallus gallus domesticus) is a domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
